field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PostgreSQL server was started and no crafted delimiter was executed; the finding is static. The upstream regression test was read, not run.

Reachability requires the application to pass an untrusted string as StringAgg's delimiter argument. StringAgg takes an explicit delimiter parameter, but not every application exposes it to user input.
The CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a) with no CVSS and no CWE. NVD and GHSA/OSV supply CWE-89 and CVSS 3.1 9.8; the canonical values come from those sources.

OSV expresses the 1.11 range as introduced 0 and the 2.x range as introduced 2.0; NVD CPE starts at 1.11 and 2.2. The 2.0-2.2 window is not represented by an NVD CPE range, so the canonical range uses the NVD/upstream branch boundaries >=2.2,<2.2.10 and records OSV's wider 2.0 start.

The fix exists as four branch-specific commits. Only the 3.0.x commit (505826b4) is an ancestor of 3.0.3; the master commit eb31d84 is not an ancestor of any fixed release tag, and the 2.2.x/1.11.x commits are ancestors of their own fixed tags. No single commit fixes all branches. MITRE and NVD cite only the master commit, which never shipped in a fixed tag.

NVD's lower bounds (>=1.11 and >=2.2) understate code-level exposure: the identical vulnerable template is present in the unsupported 1.9/1.10.8 and 2.0/2.1.15 lines as well (StringAgg was introduced in 1.9 by e4cf8c84). OSV is over-broad in the other direction: its 1.x versions list includes 1.0.1-1.8.x, which predate StringAgg. The canonical ranges stay at the NVD/upstream supported-branch boundaries, and both source defects are recorded rather than silently resolved.

Commit dates are misleading: the fix commits carry author dates (2019-12-31; 2020-01-22 for 1.11.x) that can precede the 3.0.2 tag date, yet 505826b4 is not an ancestor of 3.0.2 because it landed on the release branch after the tag was cut. Ancestry, not dates, was used.

The added regression test asserts that a single-quote delimiter survives as data; it does not assert that a syntactically hostile delimiter is rejected, so it is a targeted escaping test rather than a general injection test.
The snapshot inventory has 6163 tracked files and 67 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.
No downstream distribution backport (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, NetApp) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.

critical_operation.description: StringAgg builds its SQL from a template that embeds the caller-supplied delimiter between single quotes. StringAgg.__init__ forwards the delimiter as a raw extra kwarg; Func.__init__ stores extras in self.extra, and Func.as_sql merges self.extra into the template data and applies `template % data`, while params only collect SQL from the source expressions. The delimiter therefore becomes SQL text rather than a bound parameter, so a delimiter containing a quote can break out of the string literal and inject SQL. The 3.0.x fix replaces the template interpolation with Value(str(delimiter)), giving the delimiter its own bound parameter.

entry_point.description: An application constructs StringAgg(expression, delimiter) and the queryset compiles to SQL. The delimiter argument is the injection point when it is derived from request data; the aggregate is translated by the PostgreSQL backend through Func.as_sql.

source_crosscheck.notes: NVD, OSV/GHSA and the Django announcement agree on the three supported branches and fixed releases. The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder with no range, CVSS or CWE, so the canonical CWE-89 and 9.8 vector come from NVD/GHSA. OSV's 2.x range starts at 2.0 while NVD's CPE starts at 2.2; the upstream announcement says 2.2.x, and both agree on the 2.2.10 fixed boundary. Two range defects are recorded: NVD understates exposure because the same template exists in unsupported 1.9/1.10.8 and 2.0/2.1.15, while OSV lists 1.0.1-1.8.x even though StringAgg only appeared in 1.9. The fix is split across four branch commits, and MITRE/NVD cite only the master commit that never shipped in a fixed tag; the 3.0.x backport is the one verified against this snapshot.
